hints: Focus on what each reagent does, acid hydrolysis first, then reduction with LiAlH4.
Notice that (CH3)3CCN has four carbons in total, so hydrolysis adds the nitrile carbon into a -COOH group without adding extra carbons.
Remember that LiAlH4 reduces a carboxylic acid to -CH2OH, so think about where the OH carbon sits to decide primary, secondary or tertiary.
walkthrough:
**Identify reaction 1, hydrolysis of a nitrile**

Think of a nitrile as a masked carboxylic acid. With hot aqueous acid it hydrolyses completely.

$$\text{R-C}\equiv\text{N} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{H}^+ \rightarrow \text{R-COOH} + \text{NH}_4^+$$

**Name molecule X**

Here $\text{R} = (\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-$, so the product is $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C-COOH}$.

Count the longest chain including the $\text{COOH}$ carbon. That gives 3 carbons with two methyl branches on C2, so 2,2-dimethylpropanoic acid, given in the table as dimethylpropanoic acid.

$$ (\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CCN} \xrightarrow{\text{H}^+(aq)} (\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CCOOH} $$

**Identify reaction 2, reduction to alcohol Y**

$\text{LiAlH}_4$ is a strong reducing agent. It reduces a carboxylic acid to a primary alcohol by converting $-\text{COOH}$ to $-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$.

$$ (\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C-COOH} \xrightarrow{\text{LiAlH}_4} (\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C-CH}_2\text{OH} $$

**Classify alcohol Y**

The OH is on a carbon attached to only one other carbon ($-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$). That is the definition of a primary alcohol, even though the rest of the molecule is branched and bulky.

options.A: Incorrect because X does not gain an extra carbon. Hydrolysis converts -CN to -COOH on the same carbon skeleton, giving a 3-carbon propanoic acid, not a 4-carbon butanoic acid. The alcohol class is primary, but the name is wrong.
options.B: Incorrect on both parts. 3,3-dimethylbutanoic acid has five carbons, one more than the starting nitrile which has only four carbons in total. The product Y is $(CH3)3CCH2OH$ with -CH2OH, so primary, not tertiary.
options.C: Correct. X is (CH3)3CCOOH, which is 2,2-dimethylpropanoic acid, listed as dimethylpropanoic acid. Reduction with LiAlH4 gives (CH3)3CCH2OH, where the OH-bearing carbon is bonded to one alkyl group only, so a primary alcohol.
options.D: Half right, half wrong trap. The name dimethylpropanoic acid for X is correct, but Y is not tertiary. Students see the bulky (CH3)3C- group and think tertiary, but the OH is on a new CH2 group, so it is primary.
